newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF bid rules due soon - le Monde.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF bid rules due soon - le Monde.

text.p: The French government is set to announce the rules and constraints (cahier des charges) for the bidding for a 58-percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF on Friday or early next week, Le Monde newspaper said.
The afternoon daily also gave a joint bid by Alcatel Alsthom, Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation a good chance.
It said that Thomson-CSF Chairman Marcel Roulet had the document in hands and would discuss it at a supervisory board meeting today -- ahead of the company's 1996 results on Wednesday.

After Thomson-CSF's board meeting the text will be transmitted to the independent Privatisation Commission and then be published in the Official Journal "on Friday or more likely early next week," Le Monde said.

The paper said the "cahier des charges" would include legal and financial details on the government's aim to "assemble the biggest possible industrial capacity" in the defence sector and would allow "joint bids with a group leader".
"The offer elaborated by Alcatel Alsthom, in association with Dassault and Aerospatiale, corresponds to this definition," Le Monde said.
The paper said that a "single bid" by the Alcatel grouping and rival Lagardere, as the government had been reported to be favouring, "does not seem under consideration."

Alcatel had no comment on an earlier report in the La Tribune newspaper saying the Alcatel grouping would separate the missiles activities from Thomson-CSF and bring them into Aerospatiale, in exchange for shares in the aerospace group.
La Tribune said Alcatel would take a stake of between 51 and 70 percent in an enlarged Thomson-CSF, Dassault Industries between 10 and 15 percent and Aerospatiale between seven and 10 percent.
